gainsborough.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of West Lindsey
s1loc: Gainsborough runs its live programme from the Trinity Arts Centre, a former church on Trinity Street that stages live bands, comedy and theatre for around 200, while the medieval Gainsborough Old Hall draws heritage events beside the River Trent. The town's GO Festival fills the summer across the new Baltic Mill green space, Elswitha Green, Richmond Park and the Market Place, and Marshall's Yard hosts seasonal outdoor entertainment on its landscaped plaza.

The events trade here runs at two sizes. The arts centre, festival operators and touring production companies bring in large seasonal crews and steward teams who buy branded kit through procurement, while independent promoters, bands and single-handed event crews across West Lindsey want only a handful of pieces. A workwear supplier in this part of Lincolnshire has to fit the bigger operator and the lone crew alike, on a trade account or by direct online order.

Stewarding and front-of-house also shape the demand. A riverside event on the Trent or a parade through the Market Place needs hi-vis for marshals, weatherproof layers for gate and car-park crews, and embroidered polos that read clearly to the public. From the load-in for a Trinity Arts Centre show to the close-down of a town-centre festival, the staging, rigging and crew roles each want the right garment, named and ready for the next seasonal run.

Just along the road the Paisley Arts Centre and the new-built Beacon Arts Centre in Greenock anchor the touring circuit, while Paisley Town Hall stages headline gigs.
